messages:
Jordan: Quick thread 1: proposing we refactor the left rail into four logical clusters: Workspace (home, billing), Projects (list, settings), Models (catalog, versions), and Serving (endpoints, traffic). Goal: fewer top-level items and clearer entrypoints for new users. Thoughts?

Rina: I like the fewer-top-level idea. can we rename "Serving" to "Deployments"? engineers might find it clearer. also, what about top-level icons vs labels on small screens?

Carlos: +1 for "Deployments". Regarding deep links: we need stable URLs for bookmarks and for internal docs. prefer path-based routes like `/console/w/:wid/p/:pid/models/:mid` rather than storing UI state in query params.

Jordan: agree path-based feels cleaner. propose that only meaningful UI state (project, model, version, tab) lives in the path/query. ephemeral UI (rail collapsed/expanded) is local. when user explicitly uses "Copy link", we capture expanded group as a short fragment. example: `/console/w/w123/p/p456/models/m789#rail=projects`

Priya: accessibility notes: when a deep-link opens a model page we must programmatically move focus to the main heading and announce context, e.g. "Opened Models > m789". Also ensure collapsible groups are true accordions with `role=button` and `aria-expanded`.

Rina: microcopy: change "Workspace" to "Account"? i wonder which term maps better to billing and org-level settings. maybe test with PMs.

Carlos: from routing POV, we should avoid creating lots of redirect rules. if older routes exist, add a small compatibility layer that 302s to new canonical paths. also log when redirected so we can surface common old links.

Jordan: good call. Implementation detail: on client mount, detect deep-link with group fragment and expand the matching group synchronously before paint to avoid content jump. then call `history.replaceState` to remove fragment if it's only for UI state. pseudo: 
```js
if (fragmentIncludesRail) { expandGroup(); history.replaceState(null, '', cleanUrl); }
```

Priya: keyboard flow tests we need: arrow key nav inside rail, enter to open group, home/end jump to first/last group, and screen reader announcements when group opens. Also ensure focus trap not introduced when modal opens.

accessibility-bot: Added checklist: focus-on-load, aria-expanded, aria-current on active item, visible focus outlines, live-region announcements. Tagging #accessibility for a11y review.

Jordan: thanks — I'll sketch a low-fidelity mock showing collapsed/expanded states, clipboard-copy flow, and an example old->new redirect map. will attach tomorrow. tagging @Priya for the a11y checklist and @Carlos for the redirect plan. :thumbsup:
